s1.syndrome_frame: Malignant process of the left lower gingiva with a history of previous chemoradiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma
salient_findings: 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
Rough-surfaced polypoid lesion covered by a whitish pseudomembrane
Moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption on panoramic radiography
key_facts: 69-year-old Japanese man
Pain and a 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
History of chemoradiotherapy 15 years earlier for squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa
No recurrence until now
Denies tobacco or alcohol use
Trismus present
Intraoral inspection revealed a rough-surfaced polypoid lesion
Panoramic radiography showed a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption
Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated an enhancing soft-tissue mass with irregular mandibular bone destruction
Biopsy specimen showed loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells
Spindle cells had basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses
Immunohistochemical staining revealed positivity for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68

shortlist.label: Spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: p63 positivity indicates epithelial differentiation and history of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Sarcomatoid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells with epithelial marker negativity

shortlist.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: immunohistochemical staining revealed positivity for vimentin and CD68

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells with high Ki-67 labeling index

shortlist.label: Spindle cell melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: although less likely, cannot be completely ruled out without further testing

raw.rationale: The patient's history of chemoradiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma and the presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells with immunohistochemical staining positivity for p63, which indicates epithelial differentiation, support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While p63 positivity suggests epithelial differentiation, the lack of clear squamous cell carcinoma features and the predominance of spindle cells make this less likely

rejected.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
rejected.why: The presence of p63 positivity and the clinical context of a previous squamous cell carcinoma suggest a carcinoma rather than a pure sarcoma

rejected.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
rejected.why: The presence of epithelial markers such as p63 suggests differentiation towards carcinoma rather than a completely undifferentiated sarcoma

rejected.label: Spindle cell melanoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the immunohistochemical staining pattern do not support a diagnosis of melanoma
